books.name: Genesis
gists: God created the world, including light, land, animals, and humans.
God created man, woman, and the Garden of Eden.
Adam and Eve eat forbidden fruit, face judgment, and are expelled from Eden.
Cain kills Abel over sacrifice favoritism; God curses but spares him.
Genealogy from Adam to Noah highlights long lifespans and Enoch's faith.
Wickedness prompts God to flood the earth, sparing Noah and animals.
Noah enters the ark with his family as the flood begins.
God remembered Noah, ended the flood, and made a promise.
God establishes a covenant with Noah, promising to never flood the earth again.
Noah's sons establish nations, and Nimrod becomes a mighty hunter.
God confounds language at Babel, scattering the people.
God calls Abram to Canaan, promising descendants, blessings, and protection.
Abram and Lot separate peacefully, with Lot choosing the Jordan plain.
Abram rescues Lot from warring kings and is blessed by Melchizedek.
God promises Abram descendants and land, sealing it with a covenant.
Sarai gives Hagar to Abram; Hagar flees but is later promised descendants.
God covenants with Abraham, promising nations, land, and blessing Isaac.
God promises Abraham a son and reveals judgment on Sodom.
Angels rescue Lot before God destroys Sodom; his wife turns to salt.
Abraham lies about Sarah, leading to God's intervention and restoration.
Sarah gives birth to Isaac; Hagar and Ishmael are sent away.
Abraham shows faith by nearly sacrificing Isaac; God provides a ram instead.
Sarah dies; Abraham secures a burial site in Canaan.
Abraham's servant finds Rebekah to marry Isaac after prayer.
Abraham dies; Isaac marries Rebekah and fathers Esau and Jacob.
Isaac thrives in Gerar, faces conflict over wells, and makes a covenant.
Jacob deceives Isaac to receive Esau's blessing, prompting Esau's anger.
Jacob receives Isaac's blessing, dreams of a heavenly ladder, and names Bethel.
Jacob serves Laban for Rachel, but is deceived into marrying Leah first.
Rachel and Leah give maidservants to Jacob; he fathers more sons and prospers.
Jacob flees Laban with his family and goods, making a covenant.
Jacob wrestles with a man and becomes Israel, preparing for Esau.
Jacob reconciles with Esau and settles near Shechem.
Dinah is defiled, and her brothers avenge her through treachery.
God commands Jacob to Bethel; Rachel dies, and Isaac is buried.
Esau's descendants and Edomite chiefs are detailed, establishing his legacy.
Joseph's brothers betray him, selling him into slavery and deceiving Jacob.
Judah's lineage continues through Tamar, who bears his twins, Pharez and Zarah.
Joseph rises in Potiphar's house, resists temptation, and is imprisoned falsely.
Joseph interprets dreams in prison, predicting the butler's restoration and baker's death.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams, predicting famine and plenty; he becomes ruler.
Jacob's sons go to Egypt for grain; Joseph detains Simeon.
Israel sends sons to Egypt with Benjamin; Joseph shows favor.
Joseph tests his brothers by framing Benjamin with a stolen cup.
Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers and invites them to Egypt.
Israel moves to Egypt, reuniting with Joseph and receiving God's reassurance.
Joseph secures land for Pharaoh while bringing his family to Goshen.
Jacob blesses Joseph's sons, favoring the younger Ephraim over Manasseh.
Jacob blesses his sons, prophesying their futures before dying.
Joseph buries Jacob in Canaan and reassures his brothers.

anchors.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

books.name: Exodus
gists: Israelites grew numerous in Egypt, facing harsh oppression and infanticide edicts.
Moses is born, adopted by Pharaoh's daughter, flees to Midian, and marries.
God calls Moses from a burning bush to free Israel from Egypt.
God equips Moses and warns him about Pharaoh's hardened heart.
Moses and Aaron face Pharaoh's refusal, increasing Israel's labor suffering.
God promises Moses Israel's deliverance and commands him to confront Pharaoh.
Moses and Aaron demand Israel's release; Pharaoh's heart hardens despite miracles.
Egypt faces a frog plague and lice, but Pharaoh remains unyielding.
God sends plagues to Egypt, sparing Israel, but Pharaoh remains stubborn.
Locusts devastate Egypt; Pharaoh's temporary repentance leads to darkness.
God announces a final plague to strike Egypt, sparing Israel.
Israel marks doorposts with lamb's blood; God strikes Egypt's firstborn, leading to freedom.
God commands the sanctification of firstborns and the feast of unleavened bread.
God parts the sea, allowing Israel to escape from pursuing Egyptians.
Moses and Israel praise God for their victory and find sweet water.
Israel grumbles for food; God provides manna and quail, teaching obedience.
Israel thirsts; Moses strikes the rock for water and defeats Amalek.
Jethro advises Moses to delegate judgment to appointed leaders.
Israel prepares to receive God's covenant at Mount Sinai.
God gives the Ten Commandments, establishing law and worship guidelines.
Laws govern Hebrew servitude, punishments for offenses, and owner responsibilities.
Exodus 22 establishes laws on theft, restitution, and treating others justly.
God commands justice, care for the vulnerable, and faithfulness to His covenant.
Moses and elders worship God, covenant with Him, and Moses ascends Sinai.
God instructs Moses to gather offerings for constructing the tabernacle.
God instructs the construction details of the tabernacle.
God instructs the creation of the altar, court, and lamp.
God instructs Moses to create holy garments for consecrating priests.
God instructs the consecration of Aaron and his sons as priests.
Moses receives instructions for the altar, ransom, laver, and anointing oil.
God appoints artisans for the tabernacle and emphasizes Sabbath observance.
The Israelites worship a golden calf; Moses intercedes and punishes them.
God refuses to accompany Israel, prompting Moses to plead for His presence.
God renews the covenant and reveals His attributes to Moses.
Moses commands Sabbath observance and invites offerings for the tabernacle.
Artisans construct the tabernacle as commanded, halting excess offerings.
Bezaleel constructed sacred furniture for the Tabernacle from gold and wood.
The altar, laver, and courtyard for the tabernacle were constructed.
Israel completed the priests' garments and tabernacle furnishings for inspection.
Moses consecrates the tabernacle, priests, and God's glory fills it.

anchors.text: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.

books.name: Leviticus
gists: Israel is instructed on making voluntary burnt offerings for atonement.
Grain offerings must be fine flour, oil, and salt; priests burn part.
Peace offerings must be without blemish and properly prepared.
Sin offerings are prescribed for unintentional sins by priests and the community.
Unintentional sins require confession, offerings, and restitution for atonement.
God instructs on restitution, offerings, and maintaining the altar fire.
The LORD establishes regulations for offerings and priestly portions.
Moses consecrates Aaron and his sons for priestly duties.
Aaron offers sacrifices, and God's glory appears, igniting worship.
Nadab and Abihu die for offering unauthorized incense.
God instructs Israel on clean and unclean animals for consumption.
A mother must purify herself after childbirth and offer sacrifices.
Priests diagnose leprosy, isolate the afflicted, and re-examine after seven days.
The priest performs cleansing rituals for healed lepers and houses.
Bodily discharges cause ritual uncleanliness, requiring washings and offerings for purification.
Aaron offers sacrifices and confesses sins through a scapegoat ritual.
Sacrifices must be made at the tabernacle; eating blood is forbidden.
Israel must avoid Egypt and Canaan's practices and remain holy.
The LORD instructs Israel on holiness, justice, and community care.
God commands Israel to avoid idolatry and immorality, prescribing severe penalties.
Priests must maintain holiness and avoid ceremonial uncleanness.
The LORD commands holiness in offerings and limits participation to the clean.
God instructs Moses about Israel's sacred feasts and rest days.
God establishes laws for offerings, blasphemy punishment, and justice.
God commands land rest every seventh year and Jubilee in the fiftieth.
Obedience brings blessings; disobedience leads to destruction, but repentance restores.
Valuations and redemption rules for vows, tithes, and Jubilee fields.

anchors.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.
Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.

books.name: Numbers
gists: Moses counts Israelite warriors, excluding Levites serving the Tabernacle.
Tribes of Israel are arranged around the tabernacle for order.
Levites replace firstborns; Nadab and Abihu die for improper offerings.
Levites aged 30 to 50 are assigned specific tabernacle duties.
The unclean are removed, and a ritual for suspected adultery is established.
Instructions on the Nazarite vow and a priestly blessing for Israel.
Princes offer gifts; the altar is dedicated; God speaks to Moses.
Aaron lights lamps; Levites purified and set apart for tabernacle service.
Israel observes Passover, guided by the cloud and fire.
Moses makes trumpets, Israel departs Sinai guided by the cloud.
Israel's complaints lead to fire, quails, and a devastating plague.
Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses; God defends Moses and punishes Miriam.
Twelve spies report Canaan's bounty; fear spreads despite Caleb's encouragement to conquer.
Israel rebels, fearing the land; God condemns the generation except Joshua and Caleb.
God instructs offerings, atonement for sins, and garment fringes for remembrance.
Korah's rebellion is punished by divine fire and a plague.
Aaron's rod buds, affirming his priestly authority and preventing rebellion.
Aaron and his sons are appointed priests, assisted by the Levites.
Purification rituals using a red heifer's ashes are established.
Miriam dies, water is provided after Moses strikes a rock, and Aaron dies.
Israel battles, faces serpents, and defeats Sihon and Og.
Balak sends for Balaam to curse Israel, but God intervenes.
Balaam blesses Israel three times despite Balak's attempts to curse them.
Balaam blesses Israel, prophesying their strength and judgment on other nations.
Israelites sin, Phinehas zealously stops the plague, receiving God's covenant.
Moses counts 601,730 Israelite men for land inheritance and military service.
Zelophehad's daughters secure their inheritance; Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor.
God instructs offerings for daily, Sabbath, monthly, and festival observances.
Israel is instructed on offerings and feasts for the seventh month.
Vows are binding; husbands or fathers can nullify women's vows.
Israel defeats Midian, killing all males and dividing the spoils.
Reuben and Gad request land; promise to aid Israel in battle.
Israel's journey from Egypt details camps, Aaron's death, and God's commands.
Moses defines Canaan's borders and assigns land to the tribes.
Cities are assigned for Levites, including refuge for unintentional killers.
Gilead's daughters must marry within their tribe for inheritance.

anchors.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:

The LORD is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.
God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?

books.name: Deuteronomy
gists: Moses recounts Israel's rebellion, leading to judgment and exile.
Israel bypassed nations, defeated Sihon, and captured his land.
Israel defeats Og, dividing his land among the tribes; Moses views the Promised Land.
Moses urges Israel to obey God's laws and avoid idolatry.
Moses reiterates the Ten Commandments and Israel's fear of God's voice.
Israel must love God, keep His laws, and teach their children.
God instructs Israel to destroy nations and remain faithful to Him.
Moses urges Israel to obey God and remember His wilderness provision.
Israel is warned of their rebellion while preparing to conquer nations.
Moses renews the covenant and Israel is called to obey the LORD.
Israel must love God and follow His laws for prosperity.
Israel must worship solely at the appointed place, destroying pagan sites.
Idolatry must be punished, even among kin or cities.
Israel is called to holiness through dietary laws and tithing.
Debts are forgiven every seven years; Hebrew servants are freed.
Israel must celebrate feasts, offer joyfully, and appoint just judges.
God gives laws for worship, justice, and kings’ governance.
Levites inherit through offerings; Israel is warned against occult practices and false prophets.
Cities of refuge are established for accidental killers, ensuring justice.
Israel is instructed on warfare, reassurance, and handling besieged cities.
Cities must perform rituals for unsolved murders and address various family laws.
God sets laws on property, purity, and marriage.
Certain individuals are excluded from the congregation to maintain community purity.
Moses instructs on divorce, fair lending, and caring for the marginalized.
Justice, marriage obligations, and honest weights are mandated for Israel.
Israel brings first fruits, recounts God's deliverance, and gives tithes.
Moses instructs Israel to inscribe God's law on stones and declare blessings and curses.
Obedience brings blessings; disobedience leads to curses and judgment.
Moses urges Israel to uphold the covenant and warns of consequences.
God urges Israel to choose life through obedience and promises restoration.
Moses appoints Joshua and commands the law's public reading.
Moses sings of God's justice and Israel's unfaithfulness, foretelling judgment and mercy.
Moses blesses Israel's tribes, emphasizing God's protection and deliverance.
Moses views the Promised Land, dies, and is succeeded by Joshua.

anchors.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:

And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
